newsitem.title: INDIA: India to set up regulatory framework for energy.
newsitem.headline: India to set up regulatory framework for energy.

text.p: India is working out the details of a new regulatory framework for its energy sector, a senior government official said on Tuesday.

Legislation to establish government bodies to guide and direct the broad functioning of the players in India's petroleum and natural gas sectors is being drafted, Vijay Kelkar, the top civil servant in the Petroleum and Natural Gas Ministry, said.

"One of the new institutional arrangements emerging from the liberalisation of the energy sector is the establishment of a new Petroleum Regulatory Authority," Kelkar told delegates at a two-day seminar on oil and gas in the Indian capital.
Kelkar said the regulatory authority's role would primarily be to ensure a level playing field for all domestic and foreign private investors in India's energy sector.
It would also concern itself with the prudential aspects of oil management and good practices, he added.
"An important feature will be its duty to diffuse knowledge by creating and maintaining a geological database," Kelkar said.
Such a database would enable all players in the energy sector to plan and direct their exploration efforts efficiently.

Kelkar said his ministry was also drafting legislation to establish a new Gas Regulatory Authority. Its brief would include examining issues related to the transport of natural gas, tariff policy and pipline safety and related environmental standards, he added.

"The draft will be ready within the next two or three weeks," Kelkar said. "We will circulate it among the energy companies who have operated in India for a long time, in order to ensure that it is fair to industry and actually promotes the objectives for which it is intended."
